Title: Sign in with valid front-desk credentials
Preconditions: UAT app reachable; demo data seeded
Steps: 1) Open /login 2) Enter clinic slug, email, password 3) Submit
Expected Result: Signed in and landed on the dashboard. Left nav shows Queue, Patients, Appointments. No error banner.

Title: Sign in with a wrong password
Steps: 1) Enter valid slug and email with a wrong password 2) Submit
Expected Result: Stays on login. Message: Invalid credentials. No hint that the email exists.

Title: Sign in with an email that does not exist
Steps: 1) Enter a made-up email with any password 2) Submit
Expected Result: Same generic Invalid credentials message and a similar response time as AUTH-002 (no user enumeration).

Title: Sign in with the wrong clinic slug
Steps: 1) Enter a valid email and password but another clinic slug 2) Submit
Expected Result: Refused with Invalid credentials. A user of one clinic cannot sign in to another.

Title: Administrator is forced to enrol in MFA on first sign-in
Steps: 1) Sign in as admin 2) Observe the MFA enrolment step 3) Scan the QR / secret in an authenticator app 4) Enter the 6-digit code
Expected Result: Login returns an MFA enrolment step with a secret and QR (HTTP 200, not 401). After a valid code, the session is created and the admin lands on the dashboard.

Title: Enrolled administrator is asked for a code on later sign-ins
Steps: 1) Sign in as admin with the correct password only
Expected Result: Prompted for the 6-digit code (HTTP 200 with mfaRequired). The password step is not repeated.

Title: Wrong TOTP code is refused
Steps: 1) Sign in as admin 2) Enter 000000 as the code
Expected Result: Refused with Invalid credentials. The failure counts towards lockout.

Title: Account locks after 8 consecutive failed attempts
Preconditions: Use a throwaway account if possible
Steps: 1) Attempt sign-in with a wrong password 8 times 2) On the 9th attempt use the CORRECT password
Expected Result: From the 9th attempt onwards the correct password is also refused for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes the correct password works again.

Title: Session survives a page refresh
Steps: 1) Open the queue 2) Press F5 3) Repeat on Patients
Expected Result: The user stays signed in; no redirect to login.

Title: Access token renews silently after 15 minutes
Steps: 1) Sign in 2) Leave the tab idle for 16+ minutes 3) Click Patients and run a search
Expected Result: The action succeeds without a re-login prompt (the refresh token is valid for 7 days).

Title: Sign out clears the session
Steps: 1) Sign out 2) Press the browser Back button 3) Open /queue directly
Expected Result: Redirected to /login. Protected pages are not rendered from cache.

Title: Reusing a logged-out session is refused
Steps: 1) Sign out in tab A 2) In tab B trigger an action that needs a token refresh
Expected Result: Tab B is refused (401) and returns to login. A revoked refresh token cannot be replayed.

Title: Unauthenticated access to a protected page
Steps: 1) Open /queue, /patients and /reports/collections directly
Expected Result: Each redirects to /login. No patient data is rendered.

Title: Active sessions are listed
Steps: 1) Open the session list (Auth > sessions)
Expected Result: Both sessions appear with issue time, expiry, IP and browser.

Title: Navigation reflects the signed-in role
Steps: 1) Sign in as reception, nurse, doctor, owner, admin in turn 2) Compare the left navigation
Expected Result: Front desk: patients, appointments, queue, no Collections. Nurse: read-only, no register/book buttons, no Collections. Doctor: queue and consultations, no Collections. Owner and Admin: Collections visible.

Title: Register a patient with the minimum required fields
Steps: 1) Patients > Register 2) Enter name, gender, age, mobile 3) Tick care-delivery consent 4) Save
Expected Result: Patient created. A UHID is shown in the form SNC00001 (prefix SNC, 5 digits). Redirects to the patient record.

Title: Register using date of birth instead of age
Steps: 1) Register with a DOB and no age
Expected Result: Accepted. The record shows the DOB and derives the age.

Title: Neither date of birth nor age is rejected
Steps: 1) Register leaving both DOB and age empty
Expected Result: Validation error asking for an age or a date of birth. No patient is created.

Title: Mobile numbers are normalised to 10 digits
Steps: 1) Register three patients using different mobile formats 2) Check the stored value on each record
Expected Result: All three are stored as bare 10-digit numbers (9876500013 etc). Searching by the bare number finds them.

Title: Invalid mobile is rejected
Steps: 1) Try to register with each invalid number in turn
Expected Result: Error: mobile must be a 10-digit Indian mobile number starting 6-9. No patient created.

Title: Invalid PIN code and email are rejected
Steps: 1) Enter a 5-digit PIN 2) Enter an email without an @
Expected Result: PIN error: postalCode must be a 6-digit Indian PIN code. Email error shown on the email field.

Title: Consent is recorded for both purposes
Steps: 1) Register with care-delivery ticked and marketing UNticked 2) Open the patient record and view consents
Expected Result: Two consent rows exist: CARE_DELIVERY granted, MARKETING declined. A declined marketing consent is recorded, not omitted.

Title: Same mobile number raises a blocking duplicate warning
Steps: 1) Register a new patient using the same mobile as Ramesh Kulkarni 2) Read the warning
Expected Result: Registration is refused with a possible-duplicate warning listing the existing patient, the reason (same mobile) and their UHID.

Title: A confirmed non-duplicate can still be registered
Steps: 1) On the duplicate warning, confirm this is a different person 2) Save
Expected Result: The patient is created with a new UHID. Both records exist.

Title: A similar name alone only warns, it does not block
Steps: 1) Register with a similar name but a different mobile, gender or age
Expected Result: A weak/advisory match may be displayed, but the save goes through without a confirmation step.

Title: Extra spaces in the name are cleaned
Steps: 1) Register with double spaces and leading/trailing spaces
Expected Result: Stored as Anil Sharma (single spaces, trimmed).

Title: Age bounds
Steps: 1) Register with age 131 2) Register with age 0
Expected Result: 131 is rejected by validation. 0 is accepted (newborn).

Title: UHIDs are serial and unique
Steps: 1) Register three patients one after another 2) Note the UHIDs
Expected Result: UHIDs run consecutively with no repeats and no gaps within the run.

Title: Search by UHID, mobile, name and partial name
Steps: 1) Search the full UHID 2) Search the last 6 digits of a mobile 3) Search a full name 4) Search the first 3 letters of a name
Expected Result: Each returns the expected patient. Results show UHID, name, mobile, gender, age.

Title: Search tolerates a typo
Steps: 1) Search 'Ramesh Kulkarnee'
Expected Result: The correct patient still appears (fuzzy name match).

Title: Search needs at least 2 characters
Steps: 1) Type a single character in the search box
Expected Result: No results are returned and no error is thrown.

Title: Patient record shows demographics, consents and visit history
Preconditions: A patient with at least one completed visit
Steps: 1) Open a patient from search 2) Review every panel
Expected Result: Demographics, consent position per purpose, recent visits with doctor, date, status and token, plus totals (total visits, completed visits, last visit).

Title: Visit history is capped at 20 with an accurate total
Preconditions: A patient with more than 20 visits (create or use seeded data)
Steps: 1) Open the patient record
Expected Result: At most 20 visits are listed while the visit count reflects the true total; the page does not imply there were only 20.

Title: Nurse cannot register a patient
Steps: 1) Sign in as nurse 2) Look for the Register action 3) Open /patients/register directly
Expected Result: No Register control is shown, and reaching the page directly does not allow a save (server refuses with 403).

Title: Front desk cannot open a clinical note from the patient record
Steps: 1) Open the patient record 2) Try to open the consultation
Expected Result: The consultation is not accessible to the front desk (no link, and the direct URL is refused).

Title: Master data loads for booking
Steps: 1) Appointments > New 2) Open the department, doctor and location pickers
Expected Result: Departments (General Medicine, Paediatrics, Orthopaedics, Dermatology, ENT), the clinic's doctors and its locations are listed.

Title: Availability matches the doctor's weekly template
Steps: 1) Choose Dr Vikram Rao 2) Choose a Monday 3) Review the slots
Expected Result: Morning slots 09:00-13:00 and evening slots 17:00-20:00 in 15-minute steps. No slots outside those sessions.

Title: Availability for a day the doctor does not sit
Steps: 1) Choose Dr Vikram Rao 2) Choose a Sunday
Expected Result: No slots offered, with a reason shown rather than an empty screen.

Title: Slot lengths differ by doctor
Steps: 1) Compare availability for Dr Anjali Deshpande (10-minute) and Dr Suresh Iyer (20-minute)
Expected Result: Slot intervals match each doctor's template, not a single clinic-wide length.

Title: Book an appointment
Steps: 1) Book patient with Dr Vikram Rao for a free slot today 2) Read the confirmation screen 3) Open the queue
Expected Result: Appointment created with status Booked. The confirmation shows a large token number, which is the number the patient is given at the desk. On the board they appear under 'Yet to arrive' with that token already showing.

Title: Tokens are allocated in booking order, per doctor per day
Preconditions: Fresh clinic day, no bookings yet for Dr Rao
Steps: 1) Book three patients with Dr Rao for today, in any slot order 2) Note each token 3) Book one patient with Dr Deshpande
Expected Result: Dr Rao's three hold tokens 1, 2 and 3 in the order they were BOOKED - not in slot order. Dr Deshpande's patient holds token 1: series run per doctor, not clinic-wide.

Title: A cancelled booking leaves a gap in the token series
Steps: 1) Book two patients (tokens 1 and 2) 2) Cancel the first 3) Book a third patient
Expected Result: The third patient gets token 3, not 1. Gaps are expected - a token is an identifier, not a receipt number, and renumbering would move a token out from under a patient already holding a slip.

Title: Booking raises the bill automatically
Steps: 1) Book a NEW visit with Dr Vikram Rao 2) Open the payment dialog from the queue
Expected Result: An invoice already exists, numbered INV-0000xx, for Rs 600.00 (Dr Rao's own new-patient fee, which overrides the Rs 500 catalogue price).

Title: Follow-up visits are charged at the follow-up rate
Steps: 1) Book a FOLLOW_UP visit with Dr Vikram Rao 2) Open the invoice
Expected Result: Invoice total is Rs 350.00 and the line reads as a follow-up consultation.

Title: A time outside the schedule is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to book 08:00 for Dr Vikram Rao (before his session)
Expected Result: Refused: that time is not part of the doctor's schedule for this day. No appointment and no invoice created.

Title: A full slot is refused
Steps: 1) Book the same slot repeatedly until capacity is reached 2) Attempt one more
Expected Result: Refused with 'That slot is fully booked'.

Title: Same patient booked twice with the same doctor on the same day
Steps: 1) Book the same patient with the same doctor again for the same day
Expected Result: Refused, naming the existing appointment time. Guards against double-clicks and two receptionists.

Title: Reschedule a booked appointment
Steps: 1) Reschedule to another free slot with a reason 2) Review the patient's visit list 3) Open the queue
Expected Result: The original shows as cancelled with the reason prefixed 'Rescheduled:'. A new Booked appointment exists at the new time.

Title: Rescheduling does not leave two payable bills
Steps: 1) Open Collections > outstanding / the unpaid list 2) Look for the patient
Expected Result: The patient owes for ONE visit only. If the cancelled appointment's invoice is still listed as outstanding, raise it as a defect with both invoice numbers.

Title: A patient who has arrived cannot be rescheduled
Steps: 1) Attempt to reschedule an Arrived appointment
Expected Result: Refused: only a booked appointment that has not yet arrived can be moved.

Title: Cancel with a reason
Steps: 1) Cancel it, entering a reason
Expected Result: Status becomes Cancelled, the reason is stored and visible on the patient's visit history.

Title: A completed visit cannot be cancelled
Steps: 1) Attempt to cancel it
Expected Result: Refused: a completed visit cannot be cancelled.

Title: Mark a no-show
Preconditions: A Booked appointment whose time has passed
Steps: 1) Mark it as a no-show
Expected Result: Status becomes No show and the time is recorded. It moves out of 'Yet to arrive'.

Title: No-show cannot be applied to a patient already in the queue
Steps: 1) Attempt to mark an Arrived patient as a no-show
Expected Result: Refused with an invalid-transition message naming the current status.

Title: Walk-in with an unpaid bill holds a token but stays out of the queue
Steps: 1) Register a walk-in for Dr Vikram Rao 2) Read the confirmation 3) Observe the queue
Expected Result: The visit is created WITH a token - a walk-in is registered and booked in one act - but stays 'Booked' with an unpaid flag and is not in the waiting list. The confirmation says to collect payment and check them in, not 'added to the queue'.

Title: Walk-in enters the queue once paid, keeping the same token
Preconditions: APT-018 done, note the token number
Steps: 1) Collect the full amount 2) Check the patient in 3) Observe the queue
Expected Result: The patient appears under Waiting holding THE SAME token they were given at registration. A different number here is a defect - they are holding a slip with the first one printed on it.

Title: Duplicate walk-in is refused
Steps: 1) Register the same patient as a walk-in with the same doctor again
Expected Result: Refused, naming the token they already hold.

Title: Nurse cannot book or cancel
Steps: 1) Sign in as nurse 2) Open the appointments screen
Expected Result: Booking and cancelling controls are absent; the queue is visible read-only.

Title: Check-in is blocked while money is outstanding
Preconditions: A booked, unpaid appointment. Note its token number first.
Steps: 1) Press Check in from the queue
Expected Result: Refused with the exact amount and invoice number: 'Rs 500.00 outstanding on invoice INV-000057. Collect payment before adding them to the queue.' The patient KEEPS their token - it was issued at booking - but gets no place in the waiting list and the status stays Booked.

Title: Check-in succeeds once paid, and the token does not change
Steps: 1) Press Check in 2) Compare the token with the one noted in QUE-001
Expected Result: Status becomes Arrived, the check-in time is recorded, and the patient joins the waiting list holding the SAME token as before. Check-in grants a position, not a number.

Title: The queue does not renumber anyone at check-in
Preconditions: Three booked patients for Dr Rao holding tokens 1, 2 and 3
Steps: 1) Check them in in reverse order: token 3, then 2, then 1 2) Read the waiting list
Expected Result: All three keep their original tokens. The waiting list reads 3, 2, 1 - arrival order - which is the point: the list is ordered by who turned up, not by the number they hold.

Title: Two receptionists booking at the same moment get different tokens
Preconditions: Two browsers signed in as front desk, same doctor and day
Steps: 1) Book a patient in each browser as close to simultaneously as possible 2) Compare the two tokens
Expected Result: Two different token numbers. No duplicate, no error. (The race moved from check-in to booking when tokens moved.)

Title: A patient cannot be checked in twice
Steps: 1) Press Check in again (or replay the request)
Expected Result: Refused with a message naming the current status.

Title: A cancelled appointment cannot be checked in
Steps: 1) Attempt to check it in
Expected Result: Refused; no token is consumed.

Title: Queue board sections
Steps: 1) Open Today's queue for Dr Rao
Expected Result: Sections shown: Now serving, Waiting, Yet to arrive, Completed, Cancelled/No-show, with counts.

Title: Waiting list is ordered by arrival - not by token and not by appointment time
Steps: 1) Book patient B for 09:45 FIRST, so B holds the lower token 2) Then book patient A for 11:00 3) Check in A first, then B 4) Read the waiting list
Expected Result: A is listed above B even though B holds the lower token AND has the earlier appointment. This is the core of the change: the token identifies the patient, arrival decides the order. If the list comes out in token order, raise it as P1.

Title: The 'Yet to arrive' list stays in time order
Steps: 1) Book a late slot first, then an earlier one 2) Read the 'Yet to arrive' panel
Expected Result: Listed by appointment time, earliest first - not by token. Nobody in this panel is in the queue yet, so it reads as a diary.

Title: Average wait is blank until someone has been seen
Preconditions: Fresh day, patients waiting but none called
Steps: 1) Read the average wait indicator 2) Have the doctor call one patient 3) Re-read it
Expected Result: Before anyone is called, no average is shown (not '0 min'). After the first patient is called, a mean wait in minutes appears.

Title: Queue for another date
Steps: 1) Change the queue date to yesterday or tomorrow
Expected Result: The board shows that day's appointments; today's are not mixed in.

Title: Board refresh
Steps: 1) Check a patient in on browser A 2) Refresh on browser B
Expected Result: Browser B shows the new token and the updated counts.

Title: Times are shown in clinic time (IST)
Steps: 1) Compare a booked slot time on screen with the time chosen at booking
Expected Result: All times display in the clinic's timezone (Asia/Kolkata) regardless of the tester's machine timezone. Note: the day's queue rolls over at IST midnight - this is expected, not a defect.

Title: Send a patient for an X-ray without ending the visit
Preconditions: A patient is with the doctor (Now serving) with a consultation open
Steps: 1) On the consultation screen press 'Send for tests' 2) Enter a reason 3) Send 4) Open the queue board
Expected Result: The visit moves to 'Away for tests' showing the reason. The consulting room is free (Now serving empty) so the next patient can be called. The note stays a draft and the bill is untouched.

Title: A send-out must say what for
Steps: 1) Press 'Send for tests' 2) Leave the reason blank or type two characters 3) Try to send
Expected Result: Refused. The front desk is about to be asked what the patient is waiting for, so the reason is required.

Title: Bringing them back - 'see them next'
Preconditions: QUE-020 done, and at least one other patient waiting
Steps: 1) On the 'Away for tests' panel press 'Back at the desk' 2) Choose 'See them next' 3) Read the waiting list
Expected Result: They rejoin the waiting list AHEAD of everyone already waiting, marked 'seen next', holding the SAME token. The patient currently with the doctor is not interrupted.

Title: Bringing them back - 'queue normally'
Preconditions: A patient away for tests, others waiting
Steps: 1) Press 'Back at the desk' 2) Choose 'Add to the queue normally' 3) Read the waiting list
Expected Result: They rejoin BEHIND everyone already waiting, with no 'seen next' mark. Where they land is the desk's decision, not the software's.

Title: The round trip is one visit
Steps: 1) Note the token, the invoice number and the chief complaint before sending 2) Send for tests 3) Bring them back 4) Reopen the consultation
Expected Result: Same token, same invoice (no second bill raised), and the chief complaint typed earlier is still there in a draft note. A second invoice or a lost note is a P1 defect.

Title: Resuming the note calls them back in
Preconditions: A patient returned from tests and waiting
Steps: 1) Open their consultation from the day list 2) Look at the board
Expected Result: The board shows them as Now serving. They must not still be sitting in the waiting list while they are in the room - the next patient would never be called.

Title: Move a waiting patient to the front
Steps: 1) On the third patient press 'See next' 2) Pick a reason 3) Confirm 4) Read the list
Expected Result: They move to the top of the waiting list with a 'seen next' mark, and hovering it shows the reason. Their token does not change.

Title: Undo a flag
Steps: 1) Press 'Move back' on the flagged patient 2) Read the list
Expected Result: The mark is removed and they return to their normal position, keeping the same token and bill. Expect them BEHIND anyone who arrived earlier - normal position is by when they became ready, not by token.

Title: A later emergency does not displace an earlier promise
Steps: 1) Flag patient A as 'Back with a report' 2) A moment later flag patient B as 'Emergency' 3) Read the list
Expected Result: A stays above B. Flagged patients are served in the order they were flagged - the desk has already told A they are next, and breaking that promise is what this ordering prevents.

Title: A nurse cannot move anyone up the queue
Steps: 1) Sign in as nurse 2) Look for 'See next' on the waiting rows 3) Replay the call directly against the API
Expected Result: No control is shown, and the direct call is refused with 403 (queue:prioritise). The doctor and the front desk both have it.

Title: You cannot come back from somewhere you were never sent
Preconditions: A patient waiting who was never sent out
Steps: 1) Replay the return call directly against the API for that patient
Expected Result: Refused. This is the guard that stops 'back from tests' becoming a fast lane for whoever complains loudest.

Title: Closing out a patient who never came back
Preconditions: A patient sent for tests who has gone home
Steps: 1) Open their consultation 2) Sign it with what is recorded 3) Check the board
Expected Result: The note signs, the visit shows as completed, and they leave the 'Away for tests' panel. Without this the visit would sit open all day holding a note nobody can finish.

Title: Open a consultation for a waiting patient
Preconditions: A patient is Arrived with a token
Steps: 1) Sign in as doctor 2) Open the day list 3) Open the consultation for the top token
Expected Result: The consultation screen opens, the appointment moves to In progress and the patient shows as Now serving on the board.

Title: Cannot consult a patient who has not checked in
Steps: 1) Attempt to open the consultation
Expected Result: Refused: check the patient in before starting the consultation.

Title: Cannot consult a cancelled or no-show visit
Steps: 1) Attempt to open the consultation
Expected Result: Refused, naming the appointment status.

Title: Reopening resumes the same draft
Preconditions: A draft consultation with text typed
Steps: 1) Go back to the queue 2) Open the same consultation again
Expected Result: The same note reopens with the typed content intact. No second, empty consultation is created.

Title: Record vitals
Steps: 1) Enter vitals 2) Save
Test Data: Height 170, Weight 72, BP 120/80, Pulse 78, Temp 37.2, SpO2 98
Expected Result: Vitals are saved and displayed. BMI shows as 24.9 and is derived, not typed.

Title: Implausible vitals are refused
Steps: 1) Try each value in turn: weight 700 kg, height 10 cm, temperature 50 C, SpO2 120
Expected Result: Each is rejected with a readable message on the field. Nothing is saved.

Title: Empty vitals submission
Steps: 1) Save vitals with every field blank
Expected Result: Refused: record at least one reading.

Title: Vitals can be taken more than once in a visit
Steps: 1) Nurse records a first set 2) Doctor records a second set
Expected Result: Both sets are retained with times and recorder; the latest is shown at the top.

Title: Nurse can record vitals but cannot write the note
Steps: 1) Sign in as nurse 2) Record vitals 3) Attempt to edit the complaint, diagnosis or prescription
Expected Result: Vitals save. The narrative, diagnosis and prescription are not editable (and the direct API call is refused with 403).

Title: Write the narrative
Steps: 1) Enter chief complaint, history, examination findings, advice and a follow-up date 2) Save 3) Reopen
Expected Result: All fields persist exactly as typed, including the follow-up date.

Title: Narrative field length limits
Steps: 1) Paste 600 characters into chief complaint
Expected Result: Rejected with a length message (limit 500). Longer free-text fields accept up to 5000.

Title: ICD-10 diagnosis search
Steps: 1) Search by term 'fever' 2) Search by code 'J06'
Expected Result: Matching ICD-10 codes and descriptions are offered for both a term and a code.

Title: Exactly one diagnosis is primary, and it is the one chosen
Steps: 1) Add two diagnoses 2) Mark the SECOND one as primary 3) Save and reopen
Expected Result: The second diagnosis is flagged primary and the first is not. (Regression check - this previously snapped back to the first.)

Title: Diagnosis list cap
Steps: 1) Attempt to add 11 diagnoses
Expected Result: Rejected with a validation message at the cap of 10.

Title: Prescribe from the formulary
Steps: 1) Start typing a drug name 2) Pick from the list 3) Fill dose, frequency, duration 4) Save
Test Data: Paracetamol 500 mg, 1 tab, twice daily, 3 days
Expected Result: The prescription row saves with all structured fields separately visible.

Title: A typed-in drug is accepted and added to the clinic's list
Steps: 1) Type a drug NOT in the formulary 2) Complete the fields and save 3) Start a new prescription and search that name again
Test Data: Any brand not in the seeded list
Expected Result: The prescription saves, and on the next search the drug now appears in the clinic's list (flagged as clinic-added).

Title: Prescription without a duration or a quantity is refused
Steps: 1) Add a drug with dose and frequency but no duration and no quantity 2) Save
Expected Result: Refused, naming the drug: give a duration in days or a quantity, so the pharmacist knows how much.

Title: Prescription list cap
Steps: 1) Attempt to save 31 drugs
Expected Result: Rejected at the cap of 30.

Title: Signing an empty note is refused
Preconditions: A consultation with no complaint and no diagnosis
Steps: 1) Press Sign
Expected Result: Refused: record a complaint or a diagnosis before signing.

Title: Sign the consultation
Steps: 1) Press Sign 2) Read the note header 3) Open the queue
Expected Result: The note is marked Signed with the doctor's name and a timestamp, and the appointment becomes Completed on the board without a separate action.

Title: A signed note cannot be edited
Steps: 1) Attempt to change the complaint 2) Attempt to add a diagnosis 3) Attempt to add a prescription 4) Attempt to add vitals
Expected Result: Every attempt is refused with: this consultation is signed, add an addendum to correct it. Confirm this holds when the request is replayed directly against the API, not only in the UI.

Title: Correct a signed note with an addendum
Steps: 1) Add an addendum 2) Reopen the note
Expected Result: The addendum appears beneath the original with the author's name and time. The original text is unchanged.

Title: Addendum on a draft is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to add an addendum
Expected Result: Refused: this consultation is still a draft, edit it directly instead.

Title: Addendum minimum length
Steps: 1) Attempt an addendum of 2 characters
Expected Result: Rejected by validation (minimum 3 characters).

Title: Print the prescription
Steps: 1) Press Print 2) Inspect the preview
Expected Result: Print shows: clinic name, patient name, UHID, age/gender, date, doctor name with qualification and NMC registration number (e.g. MMC-2011-48213), every drug with dose, frequency, route and duration, advice and follow-up date. Navigation and buttons are not printed.

Title: Print when the doctor has no registration number
Preconditions: A practitioner record with the registration number cleared
Steps: 1) Sign a consultation for that doctor 2) Print
Expected Result: The print must state clearly that the registration number is missing rather than produce a document that looks valid. Raise a defect if it prints silently.

Title: Past consultations appear on the patient record
Steps: 1) Open the patient record 2) Review the visit history
Expected Result: The visit lists the date, doctor, chief complaint, primary diagnosis and the number of drugs prescribed, and opens the full note.

Title: Front desk cannot read a clinical note
Steps: 1) Sign in as reception 2) Attempt to open the consultation URL directly
Expected Result: Refused with 403. No clinical content is rendered.

Title: Invoice number format and sequence
Steps: 1) Book three appointments in a row 2) Note each invoice number
Expected Result: Numbers are INV- followed by 6 digits, consecutive, with no repeats and no gaps.

Title: The doctor's own fee overrides the catalogue price
Steps: 1) Book a new-patient visit with Dr Suresh Iyer 2) Open the invoice
Expected Result: The invoice is Rs 800.00 (Dr Iyer's fee), not the Rs 500.00 catalogue price for CONS-NEW.

Title: Add a chargeable item to an unpaid bill
Steps: 1) Open the payment dialog 2) Add 'Dressing' from the catalogue 3) Read the total
Expected Result: The line is added and the total rises by exactly Rs 250.00.

Title: Tax is applied to a taxable item only
Steps: 1) Add 'Dressing kit' (a consumable at 12%) 2) Read the line and the totals
Expected Result: Line total Rs 89.60 (Rs 80.00 + Rs 9.60 tax). The consultation line still carries no tax (healthcare services are exempt).

Title: Remove a line
Steps: 1) Remove the Dressing line
Expected Result: The line disappears and the total returns to the previous amount.

Title: A bill cannot be edited after money is taken
Preconditions: An invoice with a part payment against it
Steps: 1) Attempt to add or remove a line
Expected Result: Refused: money has been collected against this invoice, refund it before changing it.

Title: Collect the full amount in cash
Steps: 1) Collect Rs 600.00 in cash
Expected Result: Status becomes Paid, balance Rs 0.00, and the payment row shows mode Cash with the collector's name and time.

Title: Split payment across two modes
Steps: 1) Collect Rs 200.00 cash 2) Read the status 3) Collect Rs 300.00 UPI with a reference
Expected Result: After the first payment the invoice is Partially paid with Rs 300.00 outstanding; after the second it is Paid. Both rows are listed separately with their modes and the UPI reference.

Title: Overpayment is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to collect Rs 500.00
Expected Result: Refused: only Rs 300.00 is outstanding, collect that or less. No payment row is created.

Title: Zero or negative payment is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to collect Rs 0.00 2) Attempt a negative amount
Expected Result: Refused: a payment must be more than zero.

Title: Amounts with paise are exact
Preconditions: An invoice with a taxed line, e.g. total Rs 689.60
Steps: 1) Collect the exact amount 2) Check the balance and the day report
Expected Result: Balance is exactly Rs 0.00. No rounding drift of a paisa anywhere on screen or in the report.

Title: Refund part of a payment
Preconditions: A fully paid invoice of Rs 600.00
Steps: 1) Refund Rs 200.00 with a reason
Expected Result: A refund row appears, the invoice returns to Partially paid, and the outstanding balance is Rs 200.00.

Title: A refund cannot exceed what was collected
Steps: 1) Attempt to refund Rs 500.00
Expected Result: Refused: only Rs 200.00 can be refunded, that is what was actually collected.

Title: Waive a charge
Steps: 1) Waive it with a reason 2) Check the patient in
Expected Result: Status becomes Waived, the reason and the authoriser are recorded, and check-in now issues a token.

Title: A bill with money against it cannot be waived
Preconditions: An invoice with a part payment
Steps: 1) Attempt to waive it
Expected Result: Refused: the collected amount has to be refunded first.

Title: Collecting against a waived bill is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to collect a payment
Expected Result: Refused: this charge was waived, reverse the waiver before collecting.

Title: Defer payment (pay later)
Steps: 1) Defer it with a reason 2) Check the patient in 3) Open the outstanding list
Expected Result: The patient can be checked in and gets a token, and the invoice remains on the outstanding list with its reason and balance.

Title: Cancel an invoice and its effect on check-in
Preconditions: An unpaid invoice, patient not checked in
Steps: 1) Cancel the invoice with a reason 2) Attempt to check the patient in
Expected Result: Check-in is refused: invoice INV-xxxxxx was cancelled, raise a new one before checking in. The invoice is voided, never deleted, and still visible.

Title: Collecting against a cancelled invoice is refused
Steps: 1) Attempt to collect
Expected Result: Refused: this invoice was cancelled.

Title: Front desk cannot waive, defer or refund
Steps: 1) Sign in as reception 2) Open the payment dialog 3) Look for waive, defer and refund 4) Replay those API calls directly
Expected Result: No such controls are shown, and the direct API calls are refused with 403. Collection still works.

Title: Doctor holds no billing permissions
Steps: 1) Sign in as doctor 2) Look for payment controls and the Collections page
Expected Result: No billing controls anywhere; the Collections page is not reachable.

Title: Outstanding list
Preconditions: Several unpaid, partly paid and deferred invoices
Steps: 1) Open the outstanding/unpaid list
Expected Result: Shows unpaid, partly paid and deferred invoices with patient, UHID, mobile, invoice number, balance and (for deferred) the reason, most recent first.

Title: Day collection report totals
Preconditions: Several payments and one refund taken today
Steps: 1) Open Collections for today 2) Add up the transaction list by hand 3) Compare with the header totals
Expected Result: Collected, refunded and net all match the manual sum exactly. Transaction count matches the number of rows.

Title: Day collection split by mode and by collector
Preconditions: Payments taken in at least two modes by two different users
Steps: 1) Open Collections 2) Read the by-mode and by-collector panels
Expected Result: Each mode (Cash, UPI, Card, Bank transfer) and each collector shows its own collected, refunded and net, and the parts add up to the header total.

Title: Day collection for a past date
Preconditions: Payments exist on an earlier date
Steps: 1) Change the report date to that day
Expected Result: The report shows that day's transactions only, in clinic time, and today's are excluded.

Title: Collections page is not reachable without the revenue permission
Steps: 1) Sign in as reception 2) Open /reports/collections directly
Expected Result: Refused (403 / not rendered). Owner and Administrator can open it.

Title: Invoice reachable from the queue board
Steps: 1) On the queue, open the payment action for the patient
Expected Result: The bill opens showing lines, totals, payments and the balance, without leaving the queue.

Title: Pair a screen
Steps: 1) Settings > Waiting-room screens 2) Name it, choose a waiting room and optionally some doctors 3) Pair this screen 4) Copy the address
Expected Result: A web address is shown ONCE, containing a long key. The screen appears in the paired list showing its location, doctors and 'never connected'.

Title: The key is shown once and never again
Steps: 1) Press Done to dismiss the panel 2) Look for any way to see the key again 3) Reload the page
Expected Result: There is none. The key exists only as a hash in the database - a screen that loses it has to be paired afresh. If the key can be recovered anywhere in the UI, raise it as P1.

Title: The board paints on the screen
Preconditions: DSP-001 address, and a clinic day with patients
Steps: 1) Open the address on a second device or browser 2) Compare with the staff queue board
Expected Result: Shows clinic name, each doctor, the token being served in very large type, and the next few tokens. Matches the staff board's now-serving and order.

Title: No patient name is ever shown
Preconditions: A patient is with the doctor
Steps: 1) Read the whole screen carefully 2) View the page source or the network response
Expected Result: No patient name, UHID, mobile number or age anywhere - on screen OR in the underlying data. A name in the network response is a P1 defect even if the screen does not paint it.

Title: The screen follows the real queue order
Preconditions: Two patients waiting, the second holding the lower token
Steps: 1) Read the 'Next' numbers on the screen 2) Compare with the staff waiting list
Expected Result: Same order as the staff board - arrival order, not sorted token numbers.

Title: A flagged patient appears next on the screen too
Steps: 1) Flag someone 'See next' on the staff board 2) Wait about 5 seconds and read the screen
Expected Result: They appear first in 'Next'. No reason code or patient detail is shown to the room - only the number.

Title: It updates by itself
Preconditions: The screen open on a second device
Steps: 1) Call the next patient from the staff board 2) Watch the screen without touching it
Expected Result: 'Now serving' changes within about 5 seconds. Nobody has to refresh a television.

Title: It admits when it has lost the connection
Steps: 1) Stop the API (or disconnect the network) 2) Watch the screen for about 40 seconds
Expected Result: The last known board stays visible AND a 'Reconnecting - showing the board from HH:MM' banner appears. A screen that silently keeps showing stale numbers is a P1 defect; so is one that goes blank.

Title: It recovers on its own
Steps: 1) Start the API again 2) Wait about 10 seconds
Expected Result: The banner disappears and the numbers update again, with no intervention at the screen.

Title: Running late is shown honestly
Preconditions: A doctor who has not called anyone for 20+ minutes
Steps: 1) Read that doctor's panel on the screen
Expected Result: Shows 'Running late - last called N minutes ago'. It is derived from the last call, so nobody has to set or clear a flag.

Title: A wrong or mistyped address is refused
Steps: 1) Change a few characters of the key in the address 2) Open it 3) Try a nonsense address
Expected Result: Both show 'This screen is not paired' - no clinic name, no tokens, no hint about what was wrong.

Title: Turning a screen off works immediately
Steps: 1) Settings > Waiting-room screens > Turn off 2) Watch the screen
Expected Result: Within about 5 seconds it stops showing the board and says it is not paired. The entry stays in the list marked 'off' - it is not deleted.

Title: Last seen tells a dead screen from an idle one
Preconditions: A screen that has been open
Steps: 1) Open the paired list and read 'last seen'
Expected Result: A recent timestamp for a running screen; 'never connected' for one whose address was never opened.

Title: Only an administrator can pair screens
Steps: 1) Sign in as each role 2) Look for Settings > Waiting-room screens 3) Replay the pairing call directly against the API
Expected Result: The menu entry is absent for all three, and the direct call is refused with 403 (display:manage).

Title: A screen shows only its own clinic
Preconditions: A screen paired at Lotus Polyclinic, and Sunrise busy
Steps: 1) Open the Lotus screen address
Expected Result: Only Lotus doctors and tokens. No Sunrise doctor, token or clinic name appears.

Title: One clinic cannot see another clinic's patients
Preconditions: A Sunrise patient UHID and record URL noted
Steps: 1) Sign in to lotus-polyclinic 2) Search the Sunrise UHID and mobile 3) Open the Sunrise patient URL directly
Expected Result: No search results. The direct URL returns 'not found' (404) rather than 403 - the record must not be confirmed to exist.

Title: Queue, invoices and reports are clinic-scoped
Preconditions: Sunrise has appointments and invoices today
Steps: 1) In Lotus, open the queue, the outstanding list and Collections
Expected Result: Only Lotus data appears. No Sunrise appointment, invoice or payment is visible in any total.

Title: Permissions are enforced on the server, not just hidden in the UI
Preconditions: Browser dev tools or an API client
Steps: 1) As nurse, call the register-patient, book-appointment and collect-payment endpoints directly with the session cookie
Expected Result: Each returns 403. Hiding a button is not the control being tested here.

Title: Actions are written to the audit trail
Steps: 1) Register a patient, search, open a record, sign a consultation and take a payment 2) Review the audit trail
Expected Result: Each action has an entry with the actor, the time, the patient, the action name and a correlation id. Reads (patient view, search, note opened) are recorded, not only writes.

Title: Identifiable data is not exposed in URLs or errors
Steps: 1) Walk the main screens and note the URLs 2) Trigger a few errors and read the messages
Expected Result: No name, mobile or UHID in a query string. Error messages do not leak other patients' data or internal stack traces.

Title: Two receptionists booking the last free slot
Preconditions: A slot with one place left
Steps: 1) Open the booking screen in two browsers on the same slot 2) Submit both as close together as possible
Expected Result: Exactly one booking succeeds. The other is refused with 'That slot is fully booked'. No double booking and no orphan invoice.

Title: Queue board with a full day's load
Preconditions: At least 40 appointments for one doctor today
Steps: 1) Open the queue and time the load 2) Refresh a few times
Expected Result: The board renders within about 2 seconds and stays responsive. Record the timings.

Title: Patient search response
Steps: 1) Search by name, UHID and mobile, timing each
Expected Result: Results return within about 1 second each.

Title: Browser matrix
Steps: 1) Run the core flow (register, book, pay, check in, consult, sign, print) on Chrome, Edge and Safari
Expected Result: The flow completes on each browser with no layout breakage. Note any differences in the print output.

Title: Front desk on a small screen
Steps: 1) Open the queue and the payment dialog on a 1366x768 laptop and on a tablet
Expected Result: No horizontal scrolling of the page, all actions reachable, dialogs fully visible.

Title: Print layout on paper
Steps: 1) Print the prescription to A4 and to A5
Expected Result: Content fits the page, nothing is clipped, and the drug table is readable.

Title: The full clinic day, front desk to signed note
Steps: 1) Register a new patient 2) Book them with Dr Vikram Rao today and note the token on the confirmation 3) Attempt check-in (blocked) 4) Collect Rs 200 cash and Rs 400 UPI 5) Check in 6) As the doctor, open the consultation from the day list 7) Record vitals, complaint, ICD-10 diagnosis and two drugs 8) Sign 9) Print 10) As owner, open Collections
Expected Result: Every step behaves as in the individual cases. The token from step 2 is the same one on the board at step 5 and on the doctor's screen at step 6. The visit ends Completed, the note is signed and immutable, the printed prescription carries the registration number, and today's collection shows Rs 600.00 for this patient split across cash and UPI.

Title: Walk-in patient, pay later, seen and corrected
Steps: 1) Register a walk-in (no token issued) 2) As admin, defer the payment with a reason 3) Check in and note the token 4) Consult and sign 5) As doctor, add an addendum 6) As front desk, find the visit on the outstanding list and collect the money
Expected Result: The deferred visit reaches the doctor, the note is signed and corrected only by addendum, and the outstanding balance clears once collected and disappears from the outstanding list.

Title: No printed receipt for a payment
Steps: 1) Look for a print/receipt action on the invoice
Expected Result: There is none. This is a known gap, not a defect - confirm and note it only.

Title: Patient demographics cannot be edited
Steps: 1) Look for an edit action on the patient record
Expected Result: The record is read-only. Known gap; registration is the only way demographics get in.

Title: No user management or password reset
Steps: 1) Look for invite user, edit user and forgot password
Expected Result: None exist; users come from a seed. Known gap - this is the next thing being built.

Title: No appointment reminders and no patient self-booking
Steps: 1) Look for reminder settings and any patient-facing booking link
Expected Result: Neither exists (blocked on a WhatsApp provider and on the patient portal). Known gap.

Title: No drug interaction checking, lab orders, IPD, claims or ABDM
Steps: 1) Prescribe two interacting drugs 2) Look for lab orders, admissions, insurance claims and ABDM
Expected Result: No interaction warning and none of those modules exist. All deliberately out of scope for this release.
